description: Sitemap dynamic-route coverage + robust, user-updatable social handles. Ensure every dynamic route is in the generated sitemap by adding an additionalPaths generator to next-sitemap.config.js that pulls slugs from the same data sources the pages render from (sample fallback + Sanity when available), and make Organization sameAs / twitter:site robust so unconfirmed placeholder handles are not emitted as fact. Depends on FEAT-001 (baseline sitemap contents) and, for the new author pages, FEAT-002.
steps: Using FEAT-001's recorded baseline, confirm which dynamic route families next-sitemap already emits (it discovers statically-generated params from the .next app output, so pages with generateStaticParams may already be present, while CMS-only slugs and any missed families are not). The goal is a sitemap that reliably contains ALL of: /news/<article-slug>, /news/category/<cat>, /news/author/<author-slug> (new in FEAT-002), /bank-routing-numbers/<bank-slug>, /bank-routing-numbers/state, and /bank-routing-numbers/state/<state-slug>.

Add an `additionalPaths` async generator to next-sitemap.config.js (CommonJS module.exports). Because next-sitemap.config.js is plain JS and cannot import the TS data modules directly, source the slugs without duplicating data: preferred approach is to have the build emit a small JSON/JS manifest of dynamic slugs, OR require compiled data. The simplest robust approach given this repo: enumerate slugs from the TS sources by importing them through a tiny build-time helper. If direct import of TS is not feasible from the config, generate the slug lists in a committed .js data mirror is NOT acceptable (would duplicate the source of truth). Instead, evaluate migrating to a native app/sitemap.ts (Next MetadataRoute.Sitemap) which CAN import the TS data modules (data/sample-news.ts sampleArticles, data/banks.ts getAllBankSlugs/getStatesWithData, lib/us-states.ts, sampleCategories, and the FEAT-002 author list) and enumerate every dynamic route with correct loc/priority. Choose ONE approach and implement it: either (A) app/sitemap.ts as the single generator (then remove or neutralize next-sitemap so there is exactly one sitemap.xml and update the postbuild script accordingly, and keep app/robots.ts pointing at /sitemap.xml), or (B) keep next-sitemap and feed it additionalPaths via a build step that reads the real TS data (e.g. a prebuild script compiled with the project's tooling). Prefer (A) app/sitemap.ts as it reuses the exact TS data the pages render from and eliminates the static-discovery gap entirely.

If approach (A): create app/sitemap.ts exporting default function returning MetadataRoute.Sitemap. Include all static routes (/, /about, /calculators + the 7 calculator subpages, /news, /bank-routing-numbers, /bank-routing-numbers/state, /disclaimer, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-service), then map sampleArticles -> /news/<slug>, sampleCategories -> /news/category/<slug>, the author list -> /news/author/<slug>, getAllBankSlugs() -> /bank-routing-numbers/<slug>, and getStatesWithData() -> /bank-routing-numbers/state/<state.slug>. Use absolute URLs built from siteConfig.url. Preserve the priority intent from next-sitemap.config.js (/ = 1.0; /calculators, /news, /bank-routing-numbers = 0.9; others 0.7) and set changefreq/lastmod comparably. Then update package.json to drop the now-redundant `postbuild: next-sitemap` (or keep next-sitemap only if it does not also emit a conflicting sitemap.xml) and remove next-sitemap.config.js if unused. Ensure app/robots.ts still references ${siteConfig.url}/sitemap.xml (Next serves app/sitemap.ts at /sitemap.xml).

If approach (B) is chosen instead: keep next-sitemap.config.js, add additionalPaths that returns entries for every /news/<slug>, /news/category/<cat>, /news/author/<slug>, /bank-routing-numbers/<bank>, /bank-routing-numbers/state/<state> pulled from the real TS data via a compiled/prebuilt slug source (never a hand-maintained duplicate), keep the transform() priorities, and ensure no duplicate URLs are emitted for paths next-sitemap already discovers.

Centralize + harden social handles for schema. In config/site.ts, restructure `social` so each handle can be flagged as confirmed vs placeholder, OR add a clearly documented `socialConfirmed: false` gate. Simplest robust option: keep the URLs but add a boolean/comment marking them unconfirmed, and have the schema layer only emit confirmed ones. Do NOT invent new handles.

Update generateOrganizationSchema in lib/schema-markup.ts so `sameAs` only includes handles that are marked confirmed (when none are confirmed, omit `sameAs` entirely rather than emitting placeholder URLs as verified profiles). Emitting an unverified sameAs on a YMYL site is a factual-accuracy risk, so default to omitting until the user confirms. Keep a single, obvious place (config/site.ts) where the user flips the handles to confirmed once real accounts exist.

Verify there is no twitter:site/creator being emitted with an unconfirmed handle. Check app/layout.tsx and any metadata that sets a twitter handle; if a placeholder handle is used there, gate it the same way (only emit when confirmed). Report the exact locations found.
acceptance_criteria: After `npm run build`, the served sitemap.xml (public/sitemap.xml or the app/sitemap.ts output) contains at least one URL for EACH dynamic family: /news/<slug>, /news/category/<cat>, /news/author/<slug>, /bank-routing-numbers/<bank>, /bank-routing-numbers/state, /bank-routing-numbers/state/<state>, plus all static routes
Article and other slugs in the sitemap come from the same data source the pages render from (sampleArticles/banks/us-states/sampleCategories), so an empty-Sanity build still lists the sample content
Exactly one sitemap is served at /sitemap.xml (no duplicate/conflicting generators), and app/robots.ts still points at ${siteConfig.url}/sitemap.xml
generateOrganizationSchema does NOT emit placeholder social URLs in sameAs unless they are explicitly marked confirmed in config/site.ts; when none are confirmed, sameAs is omitted
No twitter:site/creator is emitted with an unconfirmed handle; config/site.ts is the single place to flip handles to confirmed
No fabricated social handles were introduced
`unset NODE_OPTIONS && npm run lint` and `unset NODE_OPTIONS && npm run build` both pass
verification: grep the generated sitemap for '/news/', '/news/category/', '/news/author/', '/bank-routing-numbers/', '/bank-routing-numbers/state' and confirm each family is present with a representative slug
grep the built output / rendered homepage JSON-LD to confirm Organization schema omits sameAs (or only emits confirmed handles)
findings:
Implemented approach (A): native app/sitemap.ts as the single sitemap generator; removed next-sitemap entirely.

PART A - Sitemap:
- CREATED app/sitemap.ts (export default function returning MetadataRoute.Sitemap). Enumerates: 16 static routes (/, /about, /calculators + all 7 calculator subpages [mortgage, 401k, emi, sip, loan-payoff, compound-interest, retirement - dir presence confirmed via ls of app/(site)/calculators], /news, /bank-routing-numbers, /bank-routing-numbers/state, /disclaimer, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-service - all dirs confirmed under app/(site)); then dynamic families from the SAME data the pages render from: sampleArticles -> /news/<slug>, sampleCategories -> /news/category/<slug>, getSampleAuthors() -> /news/author/<slug> (FEAT-002), getAllBankSlugs() -> /bank-routing-numbers/<slug>, getStatesWithData() -> /bank-routing-numbers/state/<state.slug>. Absolute URLs built from siteConfig.url (trailing slash stripped; route-group segment (site) correctly excluded). Priorities preserved from next-sitemap.config.js: /=1.0; /calculators,/news,/bank-routing-numbers=0.9; all others=0.7. changeFrequency/lastModified set reasonably; article lastModified uses publishedAt. Data shapes verified by hand: ArticleCard/Category/Author all have slug.current + publishedAt:string (lib/sanity-queries.ts lines 66-73); USState.slug is a string (lib/us-states.ts); getStatesWithData()->StateRoutingSummary{state:USState,...}.
- REMOVED next-sitemap: deleted next-sitemap.config.js (git rm), removed postbuild script and the next-sitemap dependency from package.json, updated 3 README.md references. grep confirmed the only remaining next-sitemap mentions are in lockfiles (package-lock.json/bun.lock), which are not source and were left untouched (no install possible to regenerate). Exactly one sitemap now served at /sitemap.xml via app/sitemap.ts. app/robots.ts unchanged, still points at ${siteConfig.url}/sitemap.xml. No public/sitemap.xml artifact is tracked (gitignored).
- CMS caveat: /news/[slug] and /news/category use dynamicParams default true, so Sanity-only content published post-build is not in a static sitemap either way; enumerating from sampleArticles/sampleCategories exactly matches what the pages statically render in the empty-Sanity sandbox build.

PART B - Social handles:
- config/site.ts: restructured `social` so each handle is { url, confirmed } with confirmed:false, plus a clear comment marking them placeholders and telling the user this is the single place to flip confirmed->true. No handles invented; existing URLs preserved.
- lib/schema-markup.ts generateOrganizationSchema: now derives sameAs from Object.values(siteConfig.social).filter(confirmed).map(url); sameAs is OMITTED entirely when none are confirmed (currently the case), so no placeholder profiles are emitted as fact.
- components/Footer.tsx: consumed social as strings; updated to use .url and only render each social <a> when that handle is confirmed (so the footer also stops advertising unverified accounts). This was required for type-correctness after the social restructure.
- Twitter card check: app/layout.tsx and both news twitter blocks (app/(site)/news/[slug]/page.tsx line ~65, app/(site)/news/author/[slug]/page.tsx line ~60) set only card/title/description/images - NO twitter:site or twitter:creator handle anywhere, so no gating was needed there. Reported per plan.

VERIFICATION LIMITATION: npm registry returns HTTP 403 and node_modules is missing the next/tsc binaries (confirmed: node_modules/.bin/next and .bin/tsc absent), so `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, and `tsc --noEmit` CANNOT run in this sandbox. Changes were validated by careful static/manual review against the actual TypeScript data shapes and existing patterns. Build/lint were NOT runnable and are NOT claimed to have passed.
